intro.title: Concurrent Mode Gotchas
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue application that demonstrates common pitfalls when working with asynchronous operations, such as race conditions and state update conflicts. You'll learn how to use Vue's Composition API with `ref` and `computed` to manage reactive state, and implement `watch` to handle side effects safely. The main technologies involved are Vue 3, JavaScript, and key Vue reactivity features. By the end, you'll understand how to avoid these 'gotchas' and write more predictable, concurrent-friendly code.
intro.usecase: In real-world Vue applications, concurrent mode challenges often appear when building complex dashboards with multiple live-updating widgets, such as financial trading platforms or real-time analytics interfaces. Developers encounter these gotchas when implementing interactive data filters that trigger simultaneous API calls, or when managing overlapping state updates in multi-step forms with auto-save functionality. Understanding these patterns is crucial for preventing UI flickering, race conditions, and inconsistent state in production applications where users expect smooth, predictable interactions across interconnected components.
